<section id="S4" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">4 </span>Methods</h2>

<section id="S4.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">4.1 </span>Problem formulation</h3>

<div id="S4.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We frame adaptive hit discovery as a special case of Bayesian adaptive experimental design (BAED) <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib37" title="" class="ltx_ref">37</a>]</cite>. BAED selects experiments sequentially to maximize a utility function under uncertainty. Its components are an experimental domain <math id="S4.SS1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>D</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D</annotation></semantics></math>, an observation model <math id="S4.SS1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p(y\mid d,\theta)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>y</mi><mo fence="true" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">∣</mo><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>θ</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p(y\mid d,\theta)</annotation></semantics></math> generating outcomes for a given experiment <math id="S4.SS1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>d</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d</annotation></semantics></math> and parametrized by an unknown parameter <math id="S4.SS1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\theta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>θ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta</annotation></semantics></math> with prior <math id="S4.SS1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p(\theta)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p(\theta)</annotation></semantics></math>, and a history <math id="S4.SS1.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h_{t}=\{(d_{i},y_{i})\}_{i=1}^{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>h</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><msubsup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>t</mi></msubsup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h_{t}=\{(d_{i},y_{i})\}_{i=1}^{t}</annotation></semantics></math> of past experiment–outcome pairs. At each step, the design policy <math id="S4.SS1.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pi(d_{t+1}\mid h_{t})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>π</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>d</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo fence="true" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">∣</mo><msub><mi>h</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi(d_{t+1}\mid h_{t})</annotation></semantics></math> selects the next experiment. For a fixed horizon <math id="S4.SS1.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>T</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T</annotation></semantics></math>, the optimal policy maximizes</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<table id="S4.EGx1" class="ltx_equationgroup ltx_eqn_align ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody id="S4.E1"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="S4.E1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle\pi^{*}=\operatorname*{arg\,max}_{\pi}\mathbb{E}_{\pi,p}[U(h_{T},\theta)]," display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msup><mi>π</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><munder><mrow><mi>arg</mi><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>max</mi></mrow><mi>π</mi></munder><mo>⁡</mo><msub><mi>𝔼</mi><mrow><mi>π</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>p</mi></mrow></msub></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mi>U</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>h</mi><mi>T</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle\pi^{*}=\operatorname*{arg\,max}_{\pi}\mathbb{E}_{\pi,p}[U(h_{T},\theta)],</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(1)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S4.SS1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">where <math id="S4.SS1.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="U(h_{T},\theta)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>U</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>h</mi><mi>T</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">U(h_{T},\theta)</annotation></semantics></math> is a utility function over the experimental trajectory.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS1.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS1.p3.1" class="ltx_p">Let a CRISPR screen <math id="S4.SS1.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="s" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>s</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">s</annotation></semantics></math> be composed of a natural-language description <math id="S4.SS1.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="c_{s}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>c</mi><mi>s</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c_{s}</annotation></semantics></math> of the experimental setup, a candidate gene pool <math id="S4.SS1.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{G}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒢</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{G}</annotation></semantics></math> of all possible genes (<math id="S4.SS1.p3.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="|\mathcal{G}|\approx 20{,}000" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒢</mi><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><mo>≈</mo><mn>20,000</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">|\mathcal{G}|\approx 20{,}000</annotation></semantics></math>), a screen library <math id="S4.SS1.p3.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="L\subseteq\mathcal{G}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>L</mi><mo>⊆</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒢</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">L\subseteq\mathcal{G}</annotation></semantics></math> of the genes actually measured in that screen, and binary hit labels <math id="S4.SS1.p3.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="y_{g}\in\{0,1\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>y</mi><mi>g</mi></msub><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y_{g}\in\{0,1\}</annotation></semantics></math> for each gene <math id="S4.SS1.p3.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g\in L" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi>L</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g\in L</annotation></semantics></math>. At each round <math id="S4.SS1.p3.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t\in\{1,\ldots,T\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>T</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t\in\{1,\ldots,T\}</annotation></semantics></math>, the model selects a batch <math id="S4.SS1.p3.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="B_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>B</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">B_{t}</annotation></semantics></math> of <math id="S4.SS1.p3.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="b" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>b</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">b</annotation></semantics></math> genes, observes their hit labels, and accumulates a history <math id="S4.SS1.p3.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h_{t}=\{(g,y_{g}):g\in B_{1}\cup\cdots\cup B_{t}\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>h</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>g</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mi>g</mi></msub><mo rspace="0.278em" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><msub><mi>B</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>∪</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋯</mo><mo>∪</mo><msub><mi>B</mi><mi>t</mi></msub></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h_{t}=\{(g,y_{g}):g\in B_{1}\cup\cdots\cup B_{t}\}</annotation></semantics></math>. The goal is to maximize the number of discovered hits within the fixed budget <math id="S4.SS1.p3.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T\times b" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>T</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mi>b</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T\times b</annotation></semantics></math>:</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS1.p4" class="ltx_para">
<table id="S4.EGx2" class="ltx_equationgroup ltx_eqn_align ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody id="S4.E2"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="S4.E2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle\pi^{*}=\operatorname*{arg\,max}_{\pi}\mathbb{E}_{\pi}\Big[\sum_{g\in h_{T}}y_{g}\Big]," display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msup><mi>π</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><munder><mrow><mi>arg</mi><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>max</mi></mrow><mi>π</mi></munder><mo>⁡</mo><msub><mi>𝔼</mi><mi>π</mi></msub></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo maxsize="1.600em" minsize="1.600em">[</mo><mrow><mstyle displaystyle="true"><munder><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo>∈</mo><msub><mi>h</mi><mi>T</mi></msub></mrow></munder></mstyle><msub><mi>y</mi><mi>g</mi></msub></mrow><mo maxsize="1.600em" minsize="1.600em">]</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle\pi^{*}=\operatorname*{arg\,max}_{\pi}\mathbb{E}_{\pi}\Big[\sum_{g\in h_{T}}y_{g}\Big],</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(2)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S4.SS1.p4.1" class="ltx_p">where the expectation is taken over full trajectories sampled from <math id="S4.SS1.p4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pi" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>π</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi</annotation></semantics></math>. This corresponds to the general BAED framework of Eq. <a href="#S4.E1" title="In 4.1 Problem formulation ‣ 4 Methods ‣ Biology-in-the-loop:Amortized Adaptive Hit Discovery in CRISPR Screens" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a> with a deterministic observation model <math id="S4.SS1.p4.m2" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="p(y_{g}\mid g)=\mathbb{I}[y=y_{g}]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mi>g</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.167em">∣</mo><mi>g</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mi>𝕀</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mi>g</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p(y_{g}\mid g)=\mathbb{I}[y=y_{g}]</annotation></semantics></math> and utility <math id="S4.SS1.p4.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="U(h_{T})=\sum_{g\in h_{T}}y_{g}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>U</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>h</mi><mi>T</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.111em">=</mo><mrow><msub><mo>∑</mo><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo>∈</mo><msub><mi>h</mi><mi>T</mi></msub></mrow></msub><msub><mi>y</mi><mi>g</mi></msub></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">U(h_{T})=\sum_{g\in h_{T}}y_{g}</annotation></semantics></math>. Throughout this work we use <math id="S4.SS1.p4.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T=10" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>T</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>10</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T=10</annotation></semantics></math> rounds of <math id="S4.SS1.p4.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="b=100" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>b</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>100</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">b=100</annotation></semantics></math> genes, for a total budget of 1,000 acquisitions per screen.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS1.p5" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS1.p5.1" class="ltx_p">Conventional BAED methods solve each experimental-design problem independently, fitting a task-specific probabilistic model using only observations from the current experiment <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib40" title="" class="ltx_ref">40</a>, <a href="#bib.bib27" title="" class="ltx_ref">27</a>]</cite>. Although external knowledge can be incorporated through priors, kernels, or representations, the acquisition policy itself is not learned across tasks. <em id="S4.SS1.p5.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">Amortized</em> experimental design instead learns a shared, history-conditioned policy across a distribution of tasks, moving much of the inference cost to an offline training stage and enabling knowledge transfer to new experiments <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib13" title="" class="ltx_ref">13</a>, <a href="#bib.bib3" title="" class="ltx_ref">3</a>, <a href="#bib.bib23" title="" class="ltx_ref">23</a>]</cite>. In our setting, completed large-scale CRISPR screens provide a collection of related experimental tasks from which sequential histories can be constructed retrospectively, allowing us to train an amortized acquisition policy directly from existing datasets without requiring a separate generative model.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">4.2 </span>Dataset and benchmark construction</h3>

<div id="S4.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S4.SS2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">AssayBench-Loop</span> builds upon AssayBench <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib10" title="" class="ltx_ref">10</a>]</cite>, a public benchmark containing 1,920 CRISPR screens. We adopt the same temporal train/validation/test split strategy and retain all 1,349 training screens. We use its temporal split: training screens before 2021, validation screens from 2021, and test screens after 2021. Because evaluating sequential design over multiple rounds is computationally intensive, we limit the validation and test sets to 20 screens each. These screens were selected to satisfy the following criteria: genome-wide coverage (<math id="S4.SS2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="18{,}000" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>18,000</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">18{,}000</annotation></semantics></math>–<math id="S4.SS2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="22{,}000" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>22,000</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">22{,}000</annotation></semantics></math> genes), at least 50 hits with hit rate below 15%, a non-trivial LLM performance floor (AnDCG@100 <math id="S4.SS2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\geq 0.05" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>≥</mo><mn>0.05</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\geq 0.05</annotation></semantics></math> for the best LLM from AssayBench, Gemini 3.1 Pro), phenotype distribution allocated based on the distribution of eligible test set screens, with a soft cap of six screens per category, and maximized within-phenotype diversity based on TF-IDF similarity of screen descriptions. The complete dataset composition is provided in Appendix <a href="#A1" title="Appendix A Dataset Composition ‣ Biology-in-the-loop:Amortized Adaptive Hit Discovery in CRISPR Screens" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">A</span></a>.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">4.3 </span>Evaluation metrics</h3>

<div id="S4.SS3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We let <math id="S4.SS3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{G}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒢</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{G}</annotation></semantics></math> denote the set of all possible genes, <math id="S4.SS3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="L" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>L</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">L</annotation></semantics></math> the set of genes in the gene library of a given screen (for which a label <math id="S4.SS3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="y_{g}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>y</mi><mi>g</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y_{g}</annotation></semantics></math> is available), <math id="S4.SS3.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>H</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H</annotation></semantics></math> the set of hits in <math id="S4.SS3.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="L" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>L</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">L</annotation></semantics></math>, and <math id="S4.SS3.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="G_{T}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>G</mi><mi>T</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">G_{T}</annotation></semantics></math> the set of genes acquired by the model over the <math id="S4.SS3.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>T</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T</annotation></semantics></math> rounds. Full metric definitions and implementation details are provided in Appendix <a href="#A8" title="Appendix H Metrics used in AssayBench-Loop ‣ Biology-in-the-loop:Amortized Adaptive Hit Discovery in CRISPR Screens" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">H</span></a>.</p>
</div>
<section id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Hit enrichment factor (EF).</h5>

<div id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Our primary metric measures the ratio between the number of hits found and the expected number of hits under random selection. We write <math id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N_{L}=|G_{T}\cap L|" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>N</mi><mi>L</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mrow><msub><mi>G</mi><mi>T</mi></msub><mo>∩</mo><mi>L</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N_{L}=|G_{T}\cap L|</annotation></semantics></math> for the number of acquired in-library genes, <math id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N_{\bar{\mathcal{G}}}=|G_{T}\setminus\mathcal{G}|" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>N</mi><mover accent="true"><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒢</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mrow><msub><mi>G</mi><mi>T</mi></msub><mo>∖</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒢</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N_{\bar{\mathcal{G}}}=|G_{T}\setminus\mathcal{G}|</annotation></semantics></math> for the number of hallucinated acquired genes that do not represent valid genes, and <math id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N_{\mathrm{miss}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>N</mi><mi>miss</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N_{\mathrm{miss}}</annotation></semantics></math> for the total
number of unfilled acquisition slots over the <math id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>T</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T</annotation></semantics></math> rounds. Finally, <math id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h_{\text{rand}}=|H|/|L|" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>h</mi><mtext>rand</mtext></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mi>H</mi><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><mo>/</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mi>L</mi><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h_{\text{rand}}=|H|/|L|</annotation></semantics></math> denotes the random hit rate. We define</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<table id="S4.EGx3" class="ltx_equationgroup ltx_eqn_align ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody id="S4.E3"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="S4.E3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle\mathrm{EF}=\frac{|G_{T}\cap H|}{(N_{L}+N_{\bar{\mathcal{G}}}+N_{\text{miss}})\cdot h_{\text{rand}}}." display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>EF</mi><mo>=</mo><mstyle displaystyle="true"><mfrac><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mrow><msub><mi>G</mi><mi>T</mi></msub><mo>∩</mo><mi>H</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>N</mi><mi>L</mi></msub><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>N</mi><mover accent="true"><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒢</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover></msub><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>N</mi><mtext>miss</mtext></msub></mrow><mo rspace="0.055em" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo rspace="0.222em">⋅</mo><msub><mi>h</mi><mtext>rand</mtext></msub></mrow></mfrac></mstyle></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle\mathrm{EF}=\frac{|G_{T}\cap H|}{(N_{L}+N_{\bar{\mathcal{G}}}+N_{\text{miss}})\cdot h_{\text{rand}}}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(3)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p3.1" class="ltx_p">This differs from the classical enrichment factor (<math id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="|G_{T}\cap H|/(|G_{T}|\cdot h_{\text{rand}})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mrow><msub><mi>G</mi><mi>T</mi></msub><mo>∩</mo><mi>H</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><mo>/</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><msub><mi>G</mi><mi>T</mi></msub><mo rspace="0.055em" stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><mo rspace="0.222em">⋅</mo><msub><mi>h</mi><mtext>rand</mtext></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">|G_{T}\cap H|/(|G_{T}|\cdot h_{\text{rand}})</annotation></semantics></math>) in the denominator: normalizing by <math id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(N_{L}+N_{\bar{\mathcal{G}}}+N_{\text{miss}})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>N</mi><mi>L</mi></msub><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>N</mi><mover accent="true"><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒢</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover></msub><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>N</mi><mtext>miss</mtext></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(N_{L}+N_{\bar{\mathcal{G}}}+N_{\text{miss}})</annotation></semantics></math> does not penalize acquisition of valid genes absent from the screen library but does penalize hallucinated genes and unfilled acquisition slots.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Additional metrics.</h5>

<div id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We report the normalized area under the cumulative-hits curve (nAUC), which captures the full acquisition trajectory; the fraction of hits found (FH), measuring recall; the shortfall (SF), the fraction of acquisitions falling outside the screen library; and the percentage of acquired hits that are DepMap common-essential genes (<math id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p1.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\%_{\text{ess}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>%</mo><msub><mrow></mrow><mtext>ess</mtext></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\%_{\text{ess}}</annotation></semantics></math>) <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib48" title="" class="ltx_ref">48</a>]</cite>, which separates screen-specific biology from generic cell-death phenotypes.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p2.1" class="ltx_p">We quantify the biological diversity of the acquired genes with three measures. The effective number of Reactome pathway groups (EP) is the Hill number of order 1 of the pathway distribution induced by a set of acquired genes, reported at the batch (EP-B), screen (EP-S), and dataset (EP-D) scopes <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib21" title="" class="ltx_ref">21</a>]</cite>. Within a batch, the Vendi score <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib14" title="" class="ltx_ref">14</a>]</cite> is the effective number of distinct genes under a cosine-similarity kernel over GenePT embeddings <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib7" title="" class="ltx_ref">7</a>]</cite>, reported as Vendi ratio (VR), a fraction of batch size, so that higher values indicate more diverse batches. The pathway overlap (PO) is the mean pairwise Jaccard overlap of GO biological-process annotations within a batch, divided by that of a random draw from the same library: <math id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\text{PO}=1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mtext>PO</mtext><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\text{PO}=1</annotation></semantics></math> matches random selection and <math id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\text{PO}&gt;1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mtext>PO</mtext><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\text{PO}&gt;1</annotation></semantics></math> indicates genes that share annotations. Full definitions are given in Appendix <a href="#A8" title="Appendix H Metrics used in AssayBench-Loop ‣ Biology-in-the-loop:Amortized Adaptive Hit Discovery in CRISPR Screens" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">H</span></a>.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS4" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">4.4 </span><span id="S4.SS4.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">AssayFormer</span> architecture</h3>

<div id="S4.SS4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS4.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S4.SS4.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">AssayFormer</span> is a learned acquisition policy <math id="S4.SS4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pi_{\phi}(B\mid h_{t-1},c_{s})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>π</mi><mi>ϕ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>B</mi><mo fence="true" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">∣</mo><mrow><msub><mi>h</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>c</mi><mi>s</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi_{\phi}(B\mid h_{t-1},c_{s})</annotation></semantics></math> over candidate gene batches, following the amortized design paradigm. Given a screen description <math id="S4.SS4.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="c_{s}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>c</mi><mi>s</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c_{s}</annotation></semantics></math> and the current history <math id="S4.SS4.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h_{t-1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>h</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h_{t-1}</annotation></semantics></math>, it produces per-gene acquisition scores over all untested candidates.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS4.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS4.p2.1" class="ltx_p">The model is a transformer encoder with <math id="S4.SS4.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="L=3" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>L</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">L=3</annotation></semantics></math> layers, <math id="S4.SS4.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H=2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>H</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H=2</annotation></semantics></math> attention heads, width <math id="S4.SS4.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d_{\text{model}}=384" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>d</mi><mtext>model</mtext></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>384</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d_{\text{model}}=384</annotation></semantics></math>, feed-forward dimension <math id="S4.SS4.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d_{ff}=1024" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>d</mi><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>f</mi></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>1024</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d_{ff}=1024</annotation></semantics></math>, and GELU activations. The input is a sequence of tokens comprising the experiment description (DESC) and the history gene tokens: <math id="S4.SS4.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="[\text{DESC},x_{g_{1}},\dots,x_{g_{|h_{t-1}|}}]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mtext>DESC</mtext><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><msub><mi>g</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></msub><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><msub><mi>g</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><msub><mi>h</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow></msub></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[\text{DESC},x_{g_{1}},\dots,x_{g_{|h_{t-1}|}}]</annotation></semantics></math>. No positional embeddings are applied, as gene order in the history is treated as irrelevant.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS4.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS4.p3.1" class="ltx_p">Each history gene token <math id="S4.SS4.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x_{g}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>x</mi><mi>g</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x_{g}</annotation></semantics></math> combines a learnable gene embedding <math id="S4.SS4.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="v_{g}\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{g}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>g</mi></msub><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>g</mi></msub></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">v_{g}\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{g}}</annotation></semantics></math> with a learned embedding <math id="S4.SS4.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="z_{y_{g}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>z</mi><msub><mi>y</mi><mi>g</mi></msub></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">z_{y_{g}}</annotation></semantics></math> of its binary hit label <math id="S4.SS4.p3.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="y_{g}\in\{0,1\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>y</mi><mi>g</mi></msub><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y_{g}\in\{0,1\}</annotation></semantics></math>. Separate embeddings <math id="S4.SS4.p3.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="z_{0}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>z</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">z_{0}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S4.SS4.p3.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="z_{1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>z</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">z_{1}</annotation></semantics></math> are learned for non-hits and hits, respectively. The two are concatenated and projected to the transformer latent space:</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS4.p4" class="ltx_para">
<table id="S4.Ex1" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S4.Ex1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x_{g}=W^{T}\big(v_{g}\oplus z_{y_{g}}\big)," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>x</mi><mi>g</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><msup><mi>W</mi><mi>T</mi></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>g</mi></msub><mo>⊕</mo><msub><mi>z</mi><msub><mi>y</mi><mi>g</mi></msub></msub></mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x_{g}=W^{T}\big(v_{g}\oplus z_{y_{g}}\big),</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS4.p5" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS4.p5.1" class="ltx_p">where <math id="S4.SS4.p5.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="W\in\mathbb{R}^{(d_{g}+d_{h})\times d_{\text{model}}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>W</mi><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>g</mi></msub><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>h</mi></msub></mrow><mo rspace="0.055em" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msub><mi>d</mi><mtext>model</mtext></msub></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">W\in\mathbb{R}^{(d_{g}+d_{h})\times d_{\text{model}}}</annotation></semantics></math> is a learnable projection matrix.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS4.p6" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS4.p6.1" class="ltx_p">The screen description <math id="S4.SS4.p6.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="c_{s}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>c</mi><mi>s</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c_{s}</annotation></semantics></math> is processed by first embedding it with a frozen text encoder (OpenAI <span id="S4.SS4.p6.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">text-embedding-3-small</span>), yielding <math id="S4.SS4.p6.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="e_{\text{desc}}\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{\text{text}}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>e</mi><mtext>desc</mtext></msub><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><msub><mi>d</mi><mtext>text</mtext></msub></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">e_{\text{desc}}\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{\text{text}}}</annotation></semantics></math>, and then linearly projecting it into the latent space: <math id="S4.SS4.p6.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\text{DESC}=W_{d}\,e_{\text{desc}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mtext>DESC</mtext><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>W</mi><mi>d</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>e</mi><mtext>desc</mtext></msub></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\text{DESC}=W_{d}\,e_{\text{desc}}</annotation></semantics></math>, where <math id="S4.SS4.p6.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="W_{d}\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{\text{model}}\times d_{\text{text}}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>W</mi><mi>d</mi></msub><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mrow><msub><mi>d</mi><mtext>model</mtext></msub><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msub><mi>d</mi><mtext>text</mtext></msub></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">W_{d}\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{\text{model}}\times d_{\text{text}}}</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS4.p7" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS4.p7.1" class="ltx_p">The pooled output of the DESC token through the transformer is linearly projected to the gene space to produce the screen latent <math id="S4.SS4.p7.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{u}(h_{t-1},c_{s})\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{g}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>u</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>h</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>c</mi><mi>s</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>g</mi></msub></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{u}(h_{t-1},c_{s})\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{g}}</annotation></semantics></math>. Each candidate gene <math id="S4.SS4.p7.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>g</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g</annotation></semantics></math> is scored via a bilinear head:</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS4.p8" class="ltx_para">
<table id="S4.Ex2" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S4.Ex2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a_{\phi}(g\mid h_{t-1},c_{s})\;=\;\hat{u}(h_{t-1},c_{s})^{\top}v_{g}\;+\;b_{g}," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>ϕ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>g</mi><mo fence="true" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">∣</mo><mrow><msub><mi>h</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>c</mi><mi>s</mi></msub></mrow><mo rspace="0.280em" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.558em">=</mo><mrow><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>u</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>h</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>c</mi><mi>s</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>⊤</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>g</mi></msub></mrow><mo rspace="0.502em">+</mo><msub><mi>b</mi><mi>g</mi></msub></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a_{\phi}(g\mid h_{t-1},c_{s})\;=\;\hat{u}(h_{t-1},c_{s})^{\top}v_{g}\;+\;b_{g},</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS4.p9" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS4.p9.1" class="ltx_p">where <math id="S4.SS4.p9.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="b_{g}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>b</mi><mi>g</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">b_{g}</annotation></semantics></math> is a per-gene bias. At inference time, the next batch <math id="S4.SS4.p9.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="B_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>B</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">B_{t}</annotation></semantics></math> is constructed by taking the top-<math id="S4.SS4.p9.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="b" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>b</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">b</annotation></semantics></math> previously untested genes according to <math id="S4.SS4.p9.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a_{\phi}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>ϕ</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a_{\phi}</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS5" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">4.5 </span>Training procedure</h3>

<div id="S4.SS5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Training proceeds in three stages: gene embedding initialization, supervised fine-tuning, and reinforcement learning fine-tuning.</p>
</div>
<section id="S4.SS5.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Gene embedding initialization.</h5>

<div id="S4.SS5.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS5.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We initialize the gene embeddings <math id="S4.SS5.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="v_{g}\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{g}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>g</mi></msub><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>g</mi></msub></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">v_{g}\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{g}}</annotation></semantics></math> (<math id="S4.SS5.SSS0.Px1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d_{g}=10" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>g</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>10</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d_{g}=10</annotation></semantics></math>) using a probit version of Bayesian Probabilistic Matrix Factorization (BPMF) <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib41" title="" class="ltx_ref">41</a>, <a href="#bib.bib1" title="" class="ltx_ref">1</a>]</cite>. Let <math id="S4.SS5.SSS0.Px1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Y_{ij}\in\{0,1\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>Y</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Y_{ij}\in\{0,1\}</annotation></semantics></math> indicate whether gene <math id="S4.SS5.SSS0.Px1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="j" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>j</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">j</annotation></semantics></math> scored as a hit in training screen <math id="S4.SS5.SSS0.Px1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>i</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i</annotation></semantics></math>. We model</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS5.SSS0.Px1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<table id="S4.E4" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S4.E4.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="Z_{ij}=U_{i}^{\top}V_{g_{j}}+\varepsilon_{ij},\quad\varepsilon_{ij}\sim\mathcal{N}(0,1),\qquad Y_{ij}=\mathbb{I}\left[Z_{ij}&gt;0\right]," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>Z</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><msubsup><mi>U</mi><mi>i</mi><mo>⊤</mo></msubsup><msub><mi>V</mi><msub><mi>g</mi><mi>j</mi></msub></msub><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>ε</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub><mo rspace="1.167em">,</mo><msub><mi>ε</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub><mo>∼</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒩</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo rspace="2.167em">,</mo><msub><mi>Y</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mi>𝕀</mi><mrow><mo>[</mo><msub><mi>Z</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>]</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Z_{ij}=U_{i}^{\top}V_{g_{j}}+\varepsilon_{ij},\quad\varepsilon_{ij}\sim\mathcal{N}(0,1),\qquad Y_{ij}=\mathbb{I}\left[Z_{ij}&gt;0\right],</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(4)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS5.SSS0.Px1.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS5.SSS0.Px1.p3.1" class="ltx_p">with isotropic Gaussian priors <math id="S4.SS5.SSS0.Px1.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="U_{i}\sim\mathcal{N}(0,\sigma_{u}^{2}I_{d_{g}})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>U</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>∼</mo><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒩</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi>σ</mi><mi>u</mi><mn>2</mn></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>I</mi><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>g</mi></msub></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">U_{i}\sim\mathcal{N}(0,\sigma_{u}^{2}I_{d_{g}})</annotation></semantics></math> on screen factors and <math id="S4.SS5.SSS0.Px1.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="V_{g_{j}}\sim\mathcal{N}(0,\sigma_{v}^{2}I_{d_{g}})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>V</mi><msub><mi>g</mi><mi>j</mi></msub></msub><mo>∼</mo><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒩</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi>σ</mi><mi>v</mi><mn>2</mn></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>I</mi><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>g</mi></msub></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">V_{g_{j}}\sim\mathcal{N}(0,\sigma_{v}^{2}I_{d_{g}})</annotation></semantics></math> on gene factors (<math id="S4.SS5.SSS0.Px1.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma_{u}=\sigma_{v}=1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>σ</mi><mi>u</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>σ</mi><mi>v</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma_{u}=\sigma_{v}=1</annotation></semantics></math>). Posterior distributions are estimated using Gibbs sampling with 2,000 iterations (1,000 burn-in, thinned by 2). Gene embeddings are set to the posterior mean <math id="S4.SS5.SSS0.Px1.p3.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="v_{g}=\mathbb{E}[V_{g}\mid Y]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>g</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>𝔼</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><msub><mi>V</mi><mi>g</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.167em">∣</mo><mi>Y</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">v_{g}=\mathbb{E}[V_{g}\mid Y]</annotation></semantics></math>. Genes absent from the factorization receive <math id="S4.SS5.SSS0.Px1.p3.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="v_{g}=\mathbf{0}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>g</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>𝟎</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">v_{g}=\mathbf{0}</annotation></semantics></math> and a static bias at their marginal hit frequency. Algorithmic details are provided in Appendix <a href="#A4.SS1" title="D.1 Gene embeddings initialization ‣ Appendix D Implementation details ‣ Biology-in-the-loop:Amortized Adaptive Hit Discovery in CRISPR Screens" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">D.1</span></a>. This initialization is important for downstream performance, as discussed in Appendix <a href="#A2.SS1" title="B.1 Embedding initialization ‣ Appendix B Ablations ‣ Biology-in-the-loop:Amortized Adaptive Hit Discovery in CRISPR Screens" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">B.1</span></a>.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS5.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Supervised fine-tuning.</h5>

<div id="S4.SS5.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS5.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The model is trained to predict hit labels for unobserved genes given simulated histories of varying length, using binary cross-entropy. For each training screen, a random subset <math id="S4.SS5.SSS0.Px2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{O}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒪</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{O}</annotation></semantics></math> of the screen’s genes (where <math id="S4.SS5.SSS0.Px2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="|\mathcal{O}|\sim\mathcal{U}\{0,1024\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒪</mi><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><mo>∼</mo><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒰</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1024</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">|\mathcal{O}|\sim\mathcal{U}\{0,1024\}</annotation></semantics></math>) is revealed as observed context. To ensure the model encounters informative histories, with probability 25% we resample <math id="S4.SS5.SSS0.Px2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{O}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒪</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{O}</annotation></semantics></math> to contain at least one hit: we sample <math id="S4.SS5.SSS0.Px2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n_{\text{hits}}\sim\mathcal{U}\{1,\min(|H|-1,|\mathcal{O}|)\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>n</mi><mtext>hits</mtext></msub><mo>∼</mo><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒰</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi>min</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mi>H</mi><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒪</mi><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n_{\text{hits}}\sim\mathcal{U}\{1,\min(|H|-1,|\mathcal{O}|)\}</annotation></semantics></math> and replace <math id="S4.SS5.SSS0.Px2.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n_{\text{hits}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>n</mi><mtext>hits</mtext></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n_{\text{hits}}</annotation></semantics></math> genes in <math id="S4.SS5.SSS0.Px2.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{O}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒪</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{O}</annotation></semantics></math> with randomly drawn hits, capping at <math id="S4.SS5.SSS0.Px2.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="|H|-1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mi>H</mi><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">|H|-1</annotation></semantics></math> to leave at least one hit unobserved. The model is trained on a balanced set <math id="S4.SS5.SSS0.Px2.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bar{\mathcal{O}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mover accent="true"><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒪</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bar{\mathcal{O}}</annotation></semantics></math> of unobserved genes (all unobserved hits plus an equal number of randomly sampled non-hits):</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS5.SSS0.Px2.p2" class="ltx_para">
<table id="S4.Ex3" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S4.Ex3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{L}_{\text{SFT}}\;=\;\frac{1}{|\bar{\mathcal{O}}|}\sum_{g\in\bar{\mathcal{O}}}\mathrm{BCE}\!\Big(\sigma\big(a_{\phi}(g\mid h_{t-1},c_{s})\big),\,y_{g}\Big)." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><mtext>SFT</mtext></msub><mo lspace="0.558em" rspace="0.558em">=</mo><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mover accent="true"><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒪</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><munder><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo>∈</mo><mover accent="true"><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒪</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover></mrow></munder><mrow><mpadded style="width:2.221em;" width="2.221em"><mi>BCE</mi></mpadded><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo maxsize="1.600em" minsize="1.600em">(</mo><mrow><mi>σ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>ϕ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>g</mi><mo fence="true" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">∣</mo><mrow><msub><mi>h</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>c</mi><mi>s</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mi>g</mi></msub><mo maxsize="1.600em" minsize="1.600em">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{L}_{\text{SFT}}\;=\;\frac{1}{|\bar{\mathcal{O}}|}\sum_{g\in\bar{\mathcal{O}}}\mathrm{BCE}\!\Big(\sigma\big(a_{\phi}(g\mid h_{t-1},c_{s})\big),\,y_{g}\Big).</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS5.SSS0.Px2.p3" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S4.SS5.SSS0.Px2.p3.1" class="ltx_p">This yields a greedy policy <math id="S4.SS5.SSS0.Px2.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pi_{\text{pre}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>π</mi><mtext>pre</mtext></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi_{\text{pre}}</annotation></semantics></math> that selects the <math id="S4.SS5.SSS0.Px2.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="b" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>b</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">b</annotation></semantics></math> genes with highest scores at each step.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS5.SSS0.Px3" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">RL fine-tuning.</h5>

<div id="S4.SS5.SSS0.Px3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS5.SSS0.Px3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The supervised policy is greedy and does not account for the fact that decisions at one step can influence the information gained at future steps <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib37" title="" class="ltx_ref">37</a>]</cite>. We therefore fine-tune the policy using GRPO <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib42" title="" class="ltx_ref">42</a>]</cite> on full <math id="S4.SS5.SSS0.Px3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>T</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T</annotation></semantics></math>-step trajectory rollouts. For each training screen, we perform <math id="S4.SS5.SSS0.Px3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="G=8" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>G</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>8</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">G=8</annotation></semantics></math> rollouts. Since the policy network is deterministic, rollout diversity is produced via Gumbel-top-<math id="S4.SS5.SSS0.Px3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>k</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k</annotation></semantics></math> sampling <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib26" title="" class="ltx_ref">26</a>]</cite>:</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS5.SSS0.Px3.p2" class="ltx_para">
<table id="S4.Ex4" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S4.Ex4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="B_{t}=\operatorname{Top\text{-}b}\big(\{\tilde{s}_{g}:g\notin h_{t-1}\}\big);\qquad\tilde{s}_{g}=a_{\phi}(g\mid h_{t-1},c_{s})+\tau\,\epsilon_{g},\quad\epsilon_{g}\sim\text{Gumbel}(0,1)," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>B</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>Top</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mtext>-</mtext><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>b</mi></mrow><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">(</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>s</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mi>g</mi></msub><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo>∉</mo><msub><mi>h</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="2.167em">;</mo><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>s</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mi>g</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>ϕ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>g</mi><mo fence="true" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">∣</mo><mrow><msub><mi>h</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>c</mi><mi>s</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>τ</mi><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>ϵ</mi><mi>g</mi></msub></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="1.167em">,</mo><mrow><msub><mi>ϵ</mi><mi>g</mi></msub><mo>∼</mo><mrow><mtext>Gumbel</mtext><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">B_{t}=\operatorname{Top\text{-}b}\big(\{\tilde{s}_{g}:g\notin h_{t-1}\}\big);\qquad\tilde{s}_{g}=a_{\phi}(g\mid h_{t-1},c_{s})+\tau\,\epsilon_{g},\quad\epsilon_{g}\sim\text{Gumbel}(0,1),</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS5.SSS0.Px3.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS5.SSS0.Px3.p3.1" class="ltx_p">where <math id="S4.SS5.SSS0.Px3.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau=1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>τ</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau=1</annotation></semantics></math> is the sampling temperature. Fresh noise is sampled at each acquisition step, so trajectories diverge as context accumulates.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS5.SSS0.Px3.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS5.SSS0.Px3.p4.1" class="ltx_p">The reward uses a “context delta” approach. At each step <math id="S4.SS5.SSS0.Px3.p4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>t</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math>, the reward is the difference in hits found by the context-conditioned policy relative to a frozen, context-free policy:</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS5.SSS0.Px3.p5" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<table id="S4.Ex5" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S4.Ex5.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r_{t}\;=\;\big|\{g\in B_{t}^{\pi}:y_{g}=1\}\big|\;-\;\big|\{g\in B_{t}^{\pi_{0}}:y_{g}=1\}\big|," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>r</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo lspace="0.558em" rspace="0.558em">=</mo><mrow><mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em" stretchy="true">|</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo>∈</mo><msubsup><mi>B</mi><mi>t</mi><mi>π</mi></msubsup></mrow><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mrow><msub><mi>y</mi><mi>g</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em" rspace="0.280em" stretchy="true">|</mo></mrow><mo rspace="0.502em">−</mo><mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em" stretchy="true">|</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo>∈</mo><msubsup><mi>B</mi><mi>t</mi><msub><mi>π</mi><mn>0</mn></msub></msubsup></mrow><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mrow><msub><mi>y</mi><mi>g</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em" stretchy="true">|</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r_{t}\;=\;\big|\{g\in B_{t}^{\pi}:y_{g}=1\}\big|\;-\;\big|\{g\in B_{t}^{\pi_{0}}:y_{g}=1\}\big|,</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S4.SS5.SSS0.Px3.p5.1" class="ltx_p">where <math id="S4.SS5.SSS0.Px3.p5.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="B_{t}^{\pi}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>B</mi><mi>t</mi><mi>π</mi></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">B_{t}^{\pi}</annotation></semantics></math> is the batch sampled by the current policy and <math id="S4.SS5.SSS0.Px3.p5.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="B_{t}^{\pi_{0}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>B</mi><mi>t</mi><msub><mi>π</mi><mn>0</mn></msub></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">B_{t}^{\pi_{0}}</annotation></semantics></math> is sampled from the same set of unobserved genes by the frozen policy <math id="S4.SS5.SSS0.Px3.p5.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pi_{0}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>π</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi_{0}</annotation></semantics></math> without context history. <math id="S4.SS5.SSS0.Px3.p5.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pi_{0}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>π</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi_{0}</annotation></semantics></math> is initialized by the supervised fine-tuning phase. Optionally, we update the weights of <math id="S4.SS5.SSS0.Px3.p5.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pi_{0}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>π</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi_{0}</annotation></semantics></math> from <math id="S4.SS5.SSS0.Px3.p5.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pi" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>π</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi</annotation></semantics></math> every <math id="S4.SS5.SSS0.Px3.p5.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>n</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n</annotation></semantics></math> epochs. This reward function is aligned with the hit-discovery objective in Eq. <a href="#S4.E2" title="In 4.1 Problem formulation ‣ 4 Methods ‣ Biology-in-the-loop:Amortized Adaptive Hit Discovery in CRISPR Screens" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a> while explicitly encouraging the model to exploit the revealed context to outperform the static prior. Advantages are computed as remaining returns <math id="S4.SS5.SSS0.Px3.p5.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="G_{t}^{(i)}=\sum_{s\geq t}r_{s}^{(i)}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>G</mi><mi>t</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>i</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo rspace="0.111em">=</mo><mrow><msub><mo>∑</mo><mrow><mi>s</mi><mo>≥</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow></msub><msubsup><mi>r</mi><mi>s</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>i</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">G_{t}^{(i)}=\sum_{s\geq t}r_{s}^{(i)}</annotation></semantics></math>, normalized across the group at each step. The policy is updated by the REINFORCE gradient of Plackett–Luce log-probabilities weighted by advantages, with an entropy bonus (coefficient 0.01). The fine-tuned policy <math id="S4.SS5.SSS0.Px3.p5.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pi_{\text{RL}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>π</mi><mtext>RL</mtext></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi_{\text{RL}}</annotation></semantics></math> is sampled greedily at inference time.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS6" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">4.6 </span>LLM handoff strategy</h3>

<div id="S4.SS6.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS6.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We combine the biological prior knowledge of LLMs with the adaptive capabilities of <span id="S4.SS6.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">AssayFormer</span> via a handoff strategy. For the first <math id="S4.SS6.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>k</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k</annotation></semantics></math> rounds, an LLM acts as the acquisition policy: given the screen description <math id="S4.SS6.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="c_{s}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>c</mi><mi>s</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c_{s}</annotation></semantics></math> and observed history <math id="S4.SS6.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h_{t-1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>h</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h_{t-1}</annotation></semantics></math> in context, it produces a list of <math id="S4.SS6.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="b" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>b</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">b</annotation></semantics></math> genes, providing a biologically informed warm start. We then switch to the amortized acquisition policy <math id="S4.SS6.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pi_{\text{RL}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>π</mi><mtext>RL</mtext></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi_{\text{RL}}</annotation></semantics></math> for the remaining <math id="S4.SS6.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T-k" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>T</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>k</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T-k</annotation></semantics></math> rounds, allowing the learned policy to adapt to screen-specific feedback accumulated during the warm-start phase. We select <math id="S4.SS6.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k=3" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k=3</annotation></semantics></math> on the validation set. We refer to the resulting composite policy as <span id="S4.SS6.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">AssayLoop</span>.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS7" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">4.7 </span><span id="S4.SS7.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">AssayLLM</span></h3>

<div id="S4.SS7.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS7.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S4.SS7.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">AssayLLM</span> is an LLM acquisition policy post-trained for adaptive hit discovery. At acquisition round <math id="S4.SS7.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>t</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math>, the model receives the screen description <math id="S4.SS7.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="c_{s}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>c</mi><mi>s</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c_{s}</annotation></semantics></math> and the observed history <math id="S4.SS7.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h_{t-1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>h</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h_{t-1}</annotation></semantics></math> as a multi-turn conversation, and returns a ranked list of <math id="S4.SS7.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="b" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>b</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">b</annotation></semantics></math> genes defining the next acquisition batch <math id="S4.SS7.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="B_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>B</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">B_{t}</annotation></semantics></math>. We train <span id="S4.SS7.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">AssayLLM</span> for two deployment settings: as a standalone policy controlling all <math id="S4.SS7.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>T</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T</annotation></semantics></math> acquisition rounds, and as a warm-start policy controlling the first <math id="S4.SS7.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>k</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k</annotation></semantics></math> rounds before handing the accumulated history to <span id="S4.SS7.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">AssayFormer</span>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS7.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS7.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Both variants use the 27B-parameter Qwen 3.6 backbone and share a two-stage post-training procedure. We first perform supervised fine-tuning (SFT) on acquisition trajectories and reasoning traces generated by GLM-5.1. This stage teaches the model to follow the sequential acquisition protocol, incorporate experimental feedback, avoid repeated selections, and reliably produce parseable gene batches. We then apply GRPO <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib42" title="" class="ltx_ref">42</a>]</cite> to directly optimize campaign-level hit-discovery outcomes. Rollouts from the same screen form a GRPO group, controlling for variation in screen difficulty.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS7.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS7.p3.1" class="ltx_p">To define the rewards, let <math id="S4.SS7.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="V_{t}=(B_{t}\cap L_{s})\setminus\operatorname{dom}(h_{t-1})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>V</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>B</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>∩</mo><msub><mi>L</mi><mi>s</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>∖</mo><mrow><mi>dom</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>h</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">V_{t}=(B_{t}\cap L_{s})\setminus\operatorname{dom}(h_{t-1})</annotation></semantics></math> denote the distinct, previously unobserved, in-library genes returned at round <math id="S4.SS7.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>t</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math>, and let <math id="S4.SS7.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="|H_{s}|" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><msub><mi>H</mi><mi>s</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">|H_{s}|</annotation></semantics></math> denote the total number of hits in screen <math id="S4.SS7.p3.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="s" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>s</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">s</annotation></semantics></math>. For the <math id="S4.SS7.p3.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>k</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k</annotation></semantics></math> rounds controlled by the LLM, we define</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS7.p4" class="ltx_para">

</div>
<div id="S4.SS7.p5" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS7.p5.1" class="ltx_p">Here, <math id="S4.SS7.p5.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R_{\mathrm{llm}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>R</mi><mi>llm</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R_{\mathrm{llm}}</annotation></semantics></math> measures the fraction of screen hits found directly by <span id="S4.SS7.p5.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">AssayLLM</span>, <math id="S4.SS7.p5.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="C_{\mathrm{llm}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>C</mi><mi>llm</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">C_{\mathrm{llm}}</annotation></semantics></math> measures the fraction of its acquisition budget yielding distinct scoreable observations, and <math id="S4.SS7.p5.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="F_{\mathrm{llm}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>F</mi><mi>llm</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">F_{\mathrm{llm}}</annotation></semantics></math> measures whether the model returns sufficiently complete and valid batches.</p>
</div>

<section id="S4.SS7.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Warm-start reward.</h5>

<div id="S4.SS7.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS7.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">In the warm-start setting, <span id="S4.SS7.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">AssayLLM</span> controls rounds <math id="S4.SS7.SSS0.Px2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1,\ldots,k" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>k</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1,\ldots,k</annotation></semantics></math> and the frozen <span id="S4.SS7.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">AssayFormer</span> completes rounds <math id="S4.SS7.SSS0.Px2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k+1,\ldots,T" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>T</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k+1,\ldots,T</annotation></semantics></math>. To measure handoff quality, we define</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS7.SSS0.Px2.p2" class="ltx_para">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S4.E7.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R_{\mathrm{ho}}(k,l)=\frac{1}{|H_{s}|}\sum_{t=k}^{l}\sum_{g\in V_{t}}y_{g}," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>R</mi><mi>ho</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>k</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>l</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><msub><mi>H</mi><mi>s</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><munderover><mo movablelimits="false" rspace="0em">∑</mo><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>k</mi></mrow><mi>l</mi></munderover><mrow><munder><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo>∈</mo><msub><mi>V</mi><mi>t</mi></msub></mrow></munder><msub><mi>y</mi><mi>g</mi></msub></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R_{\mathrm{ho}}(k,l)=\frac{1}{|H_{s}|}\sum_{t=k}^{l}\sum_{g\in V_{t}}y_{g},</annotation></semantics></math></td>
