</table>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS7.SSS0.Px2.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS7.SSS0.Px2.p3.1" class="ltx_p">where <math id="S4.SS7.SSS0.Px2.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="V_{k+1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>V</mi><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">V_{k+1}</annotation></semantics></math> is the first batch selected by <span id="S4.SS7.SSS0.Px2.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">AssayFormer</span> after the handoff. The warm-start reward is</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS7.SSS0.Px2.p4" class="ltx_para">
<table id="S4.E8" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S4.E8.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\begin{split}r_{\mathrm{warm}}={}&amp;w_{\mathrm{obj}}\,\mathrm{EF}+w_{\mathrm{llm}}\,R_{\mathrm{llm}}(k)+w_{\mathrm{ready}}\,R_{\mathrm{ho}}(k+1,T)\\
&amp;+w_{\mathrm{cov}}\,C_{\mathrm{llm}}(k)-w_{\mathrm{fmt}}\left(1-F_{\mathrm{llm}}(k)\right).\end{split}" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mtable columnspacing="0pt" displaystyle="true" rowspacing="0pt"><mtr><mtd class="ltx_align_right" columnalign="right"><mrow><msub><mi>r</mi><mi>warm</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mphantom></mphantom></mrow></mtd><mtd class="ltx_align_left" columnalign="left"><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>w</mi><mi>obj</mi></msub><mo lspace="0.340em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>EF</mi></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><msub><mi>w</mi><mi>llm</mi></msub><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>R</mi><mi>llm</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>k</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><msub><mi>w</mi><mi>ready</mi></msub><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>R</mi><mi>ho</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi>T</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd></mtd><mtd class="ltx_align_left" columnalign="left"><mrow><mrow><mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><msub><mi>w</mi><mi>cov</mi></msub><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>C</mi><mi>llm</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>k</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><msub><mi>w</mi><mi>fmt</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mrow><msub><mi>F</mi><mi>llm</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>k</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow></mtd></mtr></mtable><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\begin{split}r_{\mathrm{warm}}={}&amp;w_{\mathrm{obj}}\,\mathrm{EF}+w_{\mathrm{llm}}\,R_{\mathrm{llm}}(k)+w_{\mathrm{ready}}\,R_{\mathrm{ho}}(k+1,T)\\
&amp;+w_{\mathrm{cov}}\,C_{\mathrm{llm}}(k)-w_{\mathrm{fmt}}\left(1-F_{\mathrm{llm}}(k)\right).\end{split}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(8)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS7.SSS0.Px2.p5" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS7.SSS0.Px2.p5.1" class="ltx_p">The primary term <math id="S4.SS7.SSS0.Px2.p5.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{EF}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>EF</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{EF}</annotation></semantics></math> evaluates the complete LLM–<span id="S4.SS7.SSS0.Px2.p5.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">AssayFormer</span> campaign. The <math id="S4.SS7.SSS0.Px2.p5.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R_{\mathrm{llm}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>R</mi><mi>llm</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R_{\mathrm{llm}}</annotation></semantics></math> term provides direct credit for hits found during the LLM-controlled rounds, while <math id="S4.SS7.SSS0.Px2.p5.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R_{\mathrm{ho}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>R</mi><mi>ho</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R_{\mathrm{ho}}</annotation></semantics></math> credits the LLM for constructing a history that supports an effective first acquisition by <span id="S4.SS7.SSS0.Px2.p5.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">AssayFormer</span>. The <math id="S4.SS7.SSS0.Px2.p5.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="C_{\mathrm{llm}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>C</mi><mi>llm</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">C_{\mathrm{llm}}</annotation></semantics></math> term encourages distinct, scoreable observations, and the format penalty discourages degenerate batches. The auxiliary terms are important because the frozen <span id="S4.SS7.SSS0.Px2.p5.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">AssayFormer</span> may recover many readily discoverable hits regardless of the warm start, making the campaign outcome alone a weak learning signal. Additional implementation details are provided in Appendix <a href="#A4.SS4" title="D.4 AssayLLM ‣ Appendix D Implementation details ‣ Biology-in-the-loop:Amortized Adaptive Hit Discovery in CRISPR Screens" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">D.4</span></a>.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS8" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">4.8 </span>Gene-gene influence analysis</h3>

<div id="S4.SS8.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS8.p1.1" class="ltx_p">To probe what <span id="S4.SS8.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">AssayFormer</span> has learned about relationships between genes, we measure how observing one gene as a hit shifts the policy’s predicted score for another. For an ordered probe–target pair <math id="S4.SS8.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(p,g)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>p</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>g</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(p,g)</annotation></semantics></math>, we draw a synthetic background history <math id="S4.SS8.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h_{\text{bg}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>h</mi><mtext>bg</mtext></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h_{\text{bg}}</annotation></semantics></math> of <math id="S4.SS8.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="50" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>50</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">50</annotation></semantics></math> genes sampled uniformly at random from the gene vocabulary, each assigned a uniform random binary hit label, and compare the acquisition score of the target under this history with its score under the same history extended by the probe observed as a hit. The influence of <math id="S4.SS8.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>p</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p</annotation></semantics></math> on <math id="S4.SS8.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>g</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g</annotation></semantics></math> is the expected difference,</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS8.p2" class="ltx_para">
<table id="S4.E9" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S4.E9.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="I(p\to g)\;=\;\mathbb{E}_{h_{\text{bg}}}\Big[\,a_{\phi}\big(g\mid h_{\text{bg}}\cup\{(p,1)\},\,c_{s}\big)\;-\;a_{\phi}\big(g\mid h_{\text{bg}},\,c_{s}\big)\Big]," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>I</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mi>g</mi></mrow><mo rspace="0.280em" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.558em">=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>𝔼</mi><msub><mi>h</mi><mtext>bg</mtext></msub></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo maxsize="1.600em" minsize="1.600em" rspace="0.170em">[</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>ϕ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">(</mo><mi>g</mi><mo fence="true" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">∣</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>h</mi><mtext>bg</mtext></msub><mo>∪</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>p</mi><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.337em">,</mo><msub><mi>c</mi><mi>s</mi></msub></mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em" rspace="0.280em">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.502em">−</mo><mrow><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>ϕ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">(</mo><mi>g</mi><mo fence="true" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">∣</mo><mrow><msub><mi>h</mi><mtext>bg</mtext></msub><mo rspace="0.337em">,</mo><msub><mi>c</mi><mi>s</mi></msub></mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo maxsize="1.600em" minsize="1.600em">]</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">I(p\to g)\;=\;\mathbb{E}_{h_{\text{bg}}}\Big[\,a_{\phi}\big(g\mid h_{\text{bg}}\cup\{(p,1)\},\,c_{s}\big)\;-\;a_{\phi}\big(g\mid h_{\text{bg}},\,c_{s}\big)\Big],</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(9)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS8.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS8.p3.1" class="ltx_p">estimated by averaging over <math id="S4.SS8.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="10" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>10</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">10</annotation></semantics></math> independently sampled backgrounds <math id="S4.SS8.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h_{bg}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>h</mi><mrow><mi>b</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>g</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h_{bg}</annotation></semantics></math> with fixed random seeds. Because the per-gene bias <math id="S4.SS8.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="b_{g}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>b</mi><mi>g</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">b_{g}</annotation></semantics></math> is shared by both terms, the difference reduces to <math id="S4.SS8.p3.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\big(\hat{u}(h_{\text{bg}}\cup\{(p,1)\},c_{s})-\hat{u}(h_{\text{bg}},c_{s})\big)^{\top}v_{g}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">(</mo><mrow><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>u</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>h</mi><mtext>bg</mtext></msub><mo>∪</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>p</mi><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>c</mi><mi>s</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>u</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>h</mi><mtext>bg</mtext></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>c</mi><mi>s</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">)</mo></mrow><mo>⊤</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>g</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\big(\hat{u}(h_{\text{bg}}\cup\{(p,1)\},c_{s})-\hat{u}(h_{\text{bg}},c_{s})\big)^{\top}v_{g}</annotation></semantics></math>, that is, the projection of the probe-induced shift in the screen latent onto the target gene embedding. Influence is therefore directional by construction: <math id="S4.SS8.p3.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="I(p\to g)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>I</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mi>g</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">I(p\to g)</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S4.SS8.p3.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="I(g\to p)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>I</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mi>p</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">I(g\to p)</annotation></semantics></math> are separate quantities and need not agree in magnitude or sign.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS8.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS8.p4.1" class="ltx_p">Randomizing the hit labels of the background genes prevents the measurement from being dominated by a single hypothetical screen outcome, and the shared background across the two terms means that only the probe observation differs between them. All influences are computed with the RL-fine-tuned <span id="S4.SS8.p4.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">AssayFormer</span> checkpoint under a generic screen description (“A genome-wide CRISPR knockout screen to identify essential genes”), so that the reported relationships reflect structure learned across training screens rather than a single assay context. Probe or target genes absent from the model’s gene vocabulary are excluded.</p>
</div>
<section id="S4.SS8.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Screen-specific influences</h5>

<div id="S4.SS8.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS8.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">For computing screen-specific influences (Fig. <a href="#S2.SS4" title="2.4 Adaptive experimental capability scales with historical experience and transfers across phenotype categories ‣ 2 Results ‣ Biology-in-the-loop:Amortized Adaptive Hit Discovery in CRISPR Screens" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2.4</span></a>C), given a focal screen, we replace the generic screen description with the corresponding screen description <math id="S4.SS8.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="c_{s}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>c</mi><mi>s</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c_{s}</annotation></semantics></math> and set the background context <math id="S4.SS8.SSS0.Px1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h_{bg}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>h</mi><mrow><mi>b</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>g</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h_{bg}</annotation></semantics></math> to the first 100 genes selected by Gemini-3.1-Pro (given access to <math id="S4.SS8.SSS0.Px1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="c_{s}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>c</mi><mi>s</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c_{s}</annotation></semantics></math> only), together with their ground-truth hit labels.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS9" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">4.9 </span>Baselines</h3>

<section id="S4.SS9.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Adaptive experimental design methods.</h5>

<div id="S4.SS9.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS9.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We evaluate
Probability-of-Hit <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib40" title="" class="ltx_ref">40</a>]</cite> and BioBO <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib27" title="" class="ltx_ref">27</a>]</cite>,
two adaptive methods designed for CRISPR hit discovery. BioBO uses a UCB
acquisition with a biological enrichment analysis prior, while
Probability-of-Hit uses an active search acquisition function. Both use
an MLP surrogate with biologically-informed gene embeddings but do not
leverage existing CRISPR screen data.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS9.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Transfer-based baselines.</h5>

<div id="S4.SS9.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS9.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">To assess the value of learning from historical screens, we evaluate three baselines that exploit the training data: BPMF <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib41" title="" class="ltx_ref">41</a>]</cite> with a greedy acquisition function (Appendix <a href="#A4.SS1" title="D.1 Gene embeddings initialization ‣ Appendix D Implementation details ‣ Biology-in-the-loop:Amortized Adaptive Hit Discovery in CRISPR Screens" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">D.1</span></a>); Screen-kNN (Appendix <a href="#A4.SS5" title="D.5 Screen-kNN implementation ‣ Appendix D Implementation details ‣ Biology-in-the-loop:Amortized Adaptive Hit Discovery in CRISPR Screens" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">D.5</span></a>), which scores candidate genes using a distance-weighted combination of hit rates from the most similar training screens; and MAML <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib12" title="" class="ltx_ref">12</a>]</cite>, which meta-learns an initialization across training screens that can be quickly adapted via gradient steps on observed hit labels. We also include a prior-hit baseline that ranks genes by their empirical hit frequency across training screens.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS9.SSS0.Px3" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Large language models.</h5>

<div id="S4.SS9.SSS0.Px3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS9.SSS0.Px3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We evaluate several LLM families, including GLM <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib53" title="" class="ltx_ref">53</a>]</cite>, Kimi <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib47" title="" class="ltx_ref">47</a>]</cite>, Claude <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib2" title="" class="ltx_ref">2</a>]</cite>, Qwen <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib36" title="" class="ltx_ref">36</a>]</cite>, Gemini <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib16" title="" class="ltx_ref">16</a>]</cite>, and GPT <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib44" title="" class="ltx_ref">44</a>]</cite>. We adapt the prompt from AssayBench <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib10" title="" class="ltx_ref">10</a>]</cite> to the sequential setting: after each acquisition round, the accumulated experimental history, including previously selected genes and their observed hit labels, is appended to the next prompt. An example is shown in Appendix <a href="#A5.SS1" title="E.1 LLM Prompt Examples ‣ Appendix E Example Inputs ‣ Biology-in-the-loop:Amortized Adaptive Hit Discovery in CRISPR Screens" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">E.1</span></a>.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS9.SSS0.Px4" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Agentic harnesses.</h5>

<div id="S4.SS9.SSS0.Px4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS9.SSS0.Px4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We evaluate two agentic harnesses designed for adaptive hit discovery: LLMNN <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib17" title="" class="ltx_ref">17</a>]</cite>, which combines LLM prior knowledge with nearest-neighbor sampling, and ICBR-EF <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib51" title="" class="ltx_ref">51</a>]</cite>, which uses a hypothesis registry to improve in-context learning. Neither method leverages existing screen data. We therefore also evaluate a general coding agent on top of Haiku-4.5 with access to the training screens.</p>
</div>
<div class="ltx_pagination ltx_role_newpage"></div>
</section>
</section>
</section>
<section id="A1" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix A </span>Dataset Composition</h2>

<div id="A1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">AssayBench-Loop</span> builds on AssayBench <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib10" title="" class="ltx_ref">10</a>]</cite>, a public benchmark containing 1,920 CRISPR screens. We adopt the same temporal train/validation/test split and retain all 1,349 training screens. From the validation and test splits, we select 20 screens each according to the following criteria:</p>
<ol id="A1.I1" class="ltx_enumerate">
<li id="A1.I1.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">1.</span> 
<div id="A1.I1.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.I1.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.I1.i1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Genome-wide coverage</span>: the screen library contains between 18,000 and 22,000 genes.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A1.I1.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">2.</span> 
<div id="A1.I1.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.I1.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.I1.i2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Sufficient signal</span>: the screen contains at least 50 hits, with a hit rate <math id="A1.I1.i2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\leq 15\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>≤</mo><mrow><mn>15</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\leq 15\%</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A1.I1.i3" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">3.</span> 
<div id="A1.I1.i3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.I1.i3.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.I1.i3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">LLM signal floor</span>: the best LLM (Gemini-3-Pro) achieves AnDCG@100 <math id="A1.I1.i3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\geq 0.05" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>≥</mo><mn>0.05</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\geq 0.05</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A1.I1.i4" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">4.</span> 
<div id="A1.I1.i4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.I1.i4.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.I1.i4.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Phenotype stratification</span>: slots are allocated proportionally to the phenotype distribution in the eligible pool, with a soft cap of six screens per phenotype.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A1.I1.i5" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">5.</span> 
<div id="A1.I1.i5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.I1.i5.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.I1.i5.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Within-phenotype diversity</span>: screens are selected via greedy max-min TF-IDF diversity over screen descriptions (phenotype, condition, cell line, cell type, and library methodology).</p>
</div></li>
</ol>
</div>
<div id="A1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Supplementary Table <a href="#A1.T1" title="Supplementary Table 1 ‣ Appendix A Dataset Composition ‣ Biology-in-the-loop:Amortized Adaptive Hit Discovery in CRISPR Screens" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a> summarizes the phenotype distribution across splits. Supplementary Table <a href="#A1.T2" title="Supplementary Table 2 ‣ Appendix A Dataset Composition ‣ Biology-in-the-loop:Amortized Adaptive Hit Discovery in CRISPR Screens" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a> lists all 20 test screens with their key characteristics.
Because eligibility includes a minimum LLM-signal criterion, <span id="A1.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">AssayBench-Loop</span> is designed to evaluate adaptive discovery on screens for which the assay description contains detectable predictive signal, rather than to represent an unbiased sample of all genome-wide CRISPR screens.</p>
</div>
<div id="A1.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.p3.1" class="ltx_p">Please note that different sets of genes are used in different portions of the work. There is the full training vocabulary used to fit gene representations (23,724 genes), the fixed acquisition universe <math id="A1.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="G" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>G</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">G</annotation></semantics></math> used for policy rollouts and evaluation (21,147 genes appearing in at least two screens), and each screen-specific measured library <math id="A1.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="L_{s}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>L</mi><mi>s</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">L_{s}</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
<figure id="A1.T1" class="ltx_table">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering" style="font-size:90%;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table">Supplementary Table 1: </span><span id="A1.T1.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Phenotype distribution across <span id="A1.T1.5.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">AssayBench-Loop</span> splits.</span></figcaption>
<table id="A1.T1.6" class="ltx_tabular ltx_centering ltx_guessed_headers ltx_align_middle">
<thead class="ltx_thead">

<th id="A1.T1.6.1.2" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_th ltx_th_column ltx_border_tt"><span id="A1.T1.6.1.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:90%;">Train</span></th>
<th id="A1.T1.6.1.3" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_th ltx_th_column ltx_border_tt"><span id="A1.T1.6.1.3.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:90%;">Val</span></th>

</thead>
<tbody class="ltx_tbody">
<tr id="A1.T1.6.2" class="ltx_tr">
<td id="A1.T1.6.2.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_border_t"><span id="A1.T1.6.2.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Drug / Chemical / Environmental Response</span></td>
<td id="A1.T1.6.2.2" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_t"><span id="A1.T1.6.2.2.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">278</span></td>
<td id="A1.T1.6.2.3" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_t"><span id="A1.T1.6.2.3.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">6</span></td>
<td id="A1.T1.6.2.4" class="ltx_td ltx_nopad_r ltx_align_center ltx_border_t"><span id="A1.T1.6.2.4.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">6</span></td></tr>
<tr id="A1.T1.6.3" class="ltx_tr">
<td id="A1.T1.6.3.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left"><span id="A1.T1.6.3.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Fitness / Proliferation / Viability</span></td>
<td id="A1.T1.6.3.2" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center"><span id="A1.T1.6.3.2.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">947</span></td>
<td id="A1.T1.6.3.3" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center"><span id="A1.T1.6.3.3.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">6</span></td>
<td id="A1.T1.6.3.4" class="ltx_td ltx_nopad_r ltx_align_center"><span id="A1.T1.6.3.4.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">2</span></td></tr>
<tr id="A1.T1.6.4" class="ltx_tr">

<section id="A2" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix B </span>Ablations</h2>

<div id="A2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We ablate three components of <span id="A2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">AssayFormer</span>: gene embedding
initialization, the RL reward, and conditioning on the screen
description <math id="A2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="c_{s}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>c</mi><mi>s</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c_{s}</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
<section id="A2.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">B.1 </span>Embedding initialization</h3>

<div id="A2.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We compare different gene embedding initializations: BPMF (our default,
described in Section <a href="#S4.SS5" title="4.5 Training procedure ‣ 4 Methods ‣ Biology-in-the-loop:Amortized Adaptive Hit Discovery in CRISPR Screens" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4.5</span></a>), GenePT <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib7" title="" class="ltx_ref">7</a>]</cite>, Singular Value Decomposition (SVD) of the training hit
matrix, Matrix Factorization (MF) and its normalized version
(MF-Sphere), and Perturb-seq derived embeddings from the K562 cell
line <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib28" title="" class="ltx_ref">28</a>]</cite>. As shown in
Supplementary Table <a href="#A2.T3" title="Supplementary Table 3 ‣ B.2 Training strategies ‣ Appendix B Ablations ‣ Biology-in-the-loop:Amortized Adaptive Hit Discovery in CRISPR Screens" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a> (top), performance varies substantially
across embedding sources. After supervised fine-tuning, EF ranges from
<math id="A2.SS1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1.06" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>1.06</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1.06</annotation></semantics></math> (GenePT) to <math id="A2.SS1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="3.83" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>3.83</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3.83</annotation></semantics></math> (BPMF). RL fine-tuning improves all
initializations, but the gap between BPMF and alternatives widens: SVD
is close after SFT (EF <math id="A2.SS1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="3.72" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>3.72</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3.72</annotation></semantics></math> vs. <math id="A2.SS1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="3.83" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>3.83</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3.83</annotation></semantics></math>) but falls further
behind after RL (<math id="A2.SS1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="4.40" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>4.40</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4.40</annotation></semantics></math> vs. <math id="A2.SS1.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="4.83" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>4.83</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4.83</annotation></semantics></math>).</p>
</div>
<div id="A2.SS1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">In Appendix <a href="#A6.SS2" title="F.2 Embedding initialization and biological plausibility ‣ Appendix F Gene Embedding Analysis ‣ Biology-in-the-loop:Amortized Adaptive Hit Discovery in CRISPR Screens" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">F.2</span></a>, we further observe that downstream
performance does not correspond with how well the embeddings
recover canonical biological relationships from
STRING <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib46" title="" class="ltx_ref">46</a>]</cite>, CORUM <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib15" title="" class="ltx_ref">15</a>]</cite>,
SIGNOR <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib30" title="" class="ltx_ref">30</a>]</cite>, and Reactome <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib34" title="" class="ltx_ref">34</a>]</cite>,
suggesting that the structure most relevant to adaptive hit discovery
diverges from standard pathway annotations. Consistent with this, the
BPMF embeddings organize primarily by shared screen phenotype rather
than by pathway or complex membership
(Appendix <a href="#A6.SS3" title="F.3 Structure of the BPMF embedding space ‣ Appendix F Gene Embedding Analysis ‣ Biology-in-the-loop:Amortized Adaptive Hit Discovery in CRISPR Screens" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">F.3</span></a>). The BPMF geometry is also nearly
perfectly preserved during training (Pearson <math id="A2.SS1.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r=0.999" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0.999</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r=0.999</annotation></semantics></math>;
Appendix <a href="#A6.SS1" title="F.1 Embedding drift during training ‣ Appendix F Gene Embedding Analysis ‣ Biology-in-the-loop:Amortized Adaptive Hit Discovery in CRISPR Screens" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">F.1</span></a>), indicating that <span id="A2.SS1.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">AssayFormer</span> learns
on top of this structure rather than reshaping it.</p>
</div>
</section>

</figure>
<section id="A2.SS2.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">RL context-delta reward.</h5>

<div id="A2.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">During RL fine-tuning, <span id="A2.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">AssayFormer</span> is trained with the context-delta reward, which explicitly rewards
improvements over a context-free policy as experimental observations
accumulate. We validate this choice against a natural alternative:
directly optimizing the terminal EF after <math id="A2.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T=10" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>T</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>10</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T=10</annotation></semantics></math> acquisition rounds. As
shown in Supplementary Table <a href="#A2.T3" title="Supplementary Table 3 ‣ B.2 Training strategies ‣ Appendix B Ablations ‣ Biology-in-the-loop:Amortized Adaptive Hit Discovery in CRISPR Screens" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a>, the terminal EF objective
leads to worse performance. Unlike the context-delta reward, it does not
isolate the benefit of conditioning on observed history, providing a
weaker learning signal for history-dependent adaptation.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A2.SS2.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Conditioning on the screen description <math id="A2.SS2.SSS0.Px2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="c_{s}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>c</mi><mi>s</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c_{s}</annotation></semantics></math>.</h5>

<div id="A2.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Because
<span id="A2.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">AssayFormer</span> is primarily trained to adapt from accumulated experimental
observations, we test how much it relies on the initial screen
description. As shown in Supplementary Table <a href="#A2.T3" title="Supplementary Table 3 ‣ B.2 Training strategies ‣ Appendix B Ablations ‣ Biology-in-the-loop:Amortized Adaptive Hit Discovery in CRISPR Screens" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a>, removing the
screen description has relatively minor effect on performance, suggesting that
initial acquisitions are driven largely by cross-screen gene hit
patterns learned from the training data rather than the text of <math id="A2.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="c_{s}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>c</mi><mi>s</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c_{s}</annotation></semantics></math>.
This limited reliance on <math id="A2.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="c_{s}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>c</mi><mi>s</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c_{s}</annotation></semantics></math> also helps explain the complementarity of
the handoff strategy: the LLM can exploit the screen description to
provide a biologically informed warm start, while <span id="A2.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">AssayFormer</span> subsequently adapts from experimental feedback.</p>
</div>
<div class="ltx_pagination ltx_role_newpage"></div>
</section>
</section>
</section>
<section id="A3" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix C </span>Complete Results</h2>

<figure id="A3.T4" class="ltx_table">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table"><span id="A3.T4.3" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Supplementary Table 4</span>: </span><span id="A3.T4.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Full performance comparison of various baselines and ablations. Metrics evaluate enrichment factor (EF, hit rate relative to random), normalized Area Under the Curve (nAUC), fraction of hits found, mean shortfall, Vendi ratio, and batch pathway overlap versus random. EP-B/EP-S/EP-D are the effective number of Reactome level-2 pathway groups covered (186 in the vocabulary), at batch, screen and dataset scope: each gene is assigned to one of its groups at random, and the scope is subsampled to a fixed annotated-gene count (30, 200 and 6000 respectively), so the three are not directly comparable to one another.</span></figcaption>

<section id="A4" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix D </span>Implementation details</h2>

<section id="A4.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">D.1 </span>Gene embeddings initialization</h3>

<div id="A4.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Let <math id="A4.SS1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Y_{ij}\in\{0,1\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>Y</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Y_{ij}\in\{0,1\}</annotation></semantics></math> indicate
whether gene <math id="A4.SS1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="j" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>j</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">j</annotation></semantics></math> scored as a hit in screen <math id="A4.SS1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>i</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i</annotation></semantics></math>, observed on the set <math id="A4.SS1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{O}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒪</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{O}</annotation></semantics></math>
of screen–gene pairs actually assayed (<math id="A4.SS1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N=1{,}349" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1,349</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N=1{,}349</annotation></semantics></math> training screens,
<math id="A4.SS1.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M=23{,}724" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>M</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>23,724</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M=23{,}724</annotation></semantics></math> genes (the total number in our training data), <math id="A4.SS1.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="64\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>64</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">64\%</annotation></semantics></math> of pairs observed, overall hit rate <math id="A4.SS1.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="7.3\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>7.3</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">7.3\%</annotation></semantics></math>). Each
entry is generated by a latent utility</p>
<table id="A4.E10" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A4.E10.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="Z_{ij}=U_{i}^{\top}V_{g_{j}}+\varepsilon_{ij},\quad\varepsilon_{ij}\sim\mathcal{N}(0,1),\qquad Y_{ij}=\mathbb{I}\!\left[Z_{ij}&gt;0\right]," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>Z</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><msubsup><mi>U</mi><mi>i</mi><mo>⊤</mo></msubsup><msub><mi>V</mi><msub><mi>g</mi><mi>j</mi></msub></msub><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>ε</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub><mo rspace="1.167em">,</mo><msub><mi>ε</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub><mo>∼</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒩</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo rspace="2.167em">,</mo><msub><mi>Y</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mpadded style="width:0.219em;" width="0.219em"><mi>𝕀</mi></mpadded><mrow><mo>[</mo><msub><mi>Z</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>]</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Z_{ij}=U_{i}^{\top}V_{g_{j}}+\varepsilon_{ij},\quad\varepsilon_{ij}\sim\mathcal{N}(0,1),\qquad Y_{ij}=\mathbb{I}\!\left[Z_{ij}&gt;0\right],</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(10)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A4.SS1.p1.2" class="ltx_p">with isotropic Gaussian priors <math id="A4.SS1.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="U_{i}\sim\mathcal{N}(0,\sigma_{u}^{2}I_{d_{g}})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>U</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>∼</mo><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒩</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi>σ</mi><mi>u</mi><mn>2</mn></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>I</mi><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>g</mi></msub></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">U_{i}\sim\mathcal{N}(0,\sigma_{u}^{2}I_{d_{g}})</annotation></semantics></math> on the
screen factors and <math id="A4.SS1.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="V_{g_{j}}\sim\mathcal{N}(0,\sigma_{v}^{2}I_{d_{g}})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>V</mi><msub><mi>g</mi><mi>j</mi></msub></msub><mo>∼</mo><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒩</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi>σ</mi><mi>v</mi><mn>2</mn></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>I</mi><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>g</mi></msub></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">V_{g_{j}}\sim\mathcal{N}(0,\sigma_{v}^{2}I_{d_{g}})</annotation></semantics></math> on the gene
factors (<math id="A4.SS1.p1.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma_{u}=\sigma_{v}=1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>σ</mi><mi>u</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>σ</mi><mi>v</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma_{u}=\sigma_{v}=1</annotation></semantics></math>). Conditioning on <math id="A4.SS1.p1.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Z" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>Z</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Z</annotation></semantics></math> renders both factor updates
conjugate, so we alternate three Gibbs steps: <math id="A4.SS1.p1.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Z\mid Y,U,V" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>Z</mi><mo fence="false">|</mo><mrow><mi>Y</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>U</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>V</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Z\mid Y,U,V</annotation></semantics></math> drawn from
unit-variance normals truncated at zero by the sign of <math id="A4.SS1.p1.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Y" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>Y</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Y</annotation></semantics></math>
<cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib1" title="" class="ltx_ref">1</a>]</cite>, followed by</p>
<table id="A4.E11" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A4.E11.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="U_{i}\mid Z,V\;\sim\;\mathcal{N}\!\left(\Lambda_{i}^{-1}\!\!\!\sum_{j:(i,j)\in\mathcal{O}}\!\!\!V_{g_{j}}Z_{ij},\;\;\Lambda_{i}^{-1}\right),\qquad\Lambda_{i}=\!\!\!\sum_{j:(i,j)\in\mathcal{O}}\!\!\!V_{g_{j}}V_{g_{j}}^{\top}+\sigma_{u}^{-2}I_{d_{g}}," rspace="0.558em">∼</mo><mpadded style="width:0.798em;" width="0.798em"><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒩</mi></mpadded><mrow><mo>(</mo><msubsup><mi stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>i</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>j</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>∈</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒪</mi></mrow></mrow></munder><msub><mi>V</mi><msub><mi>g</mi><mi>j</mi></msub></msub><msub><mi>Z</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub><mo rspace="0.727em">,</mo><msubsup><mi mathvariant="normal">Λ</mi><mi>i</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msubsup><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo rspace="2.167em">,</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Λ</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mpadded style="width:0.546em;" width="0.546em"><mo>=</mo></mpadded><munder><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mrow><mi>j</mi><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>i</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>j</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>∈</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒪</mi></mrow></mrow></munder><msub><mi>V</mi><msub><mi>g</mi><mi>j</mi></msub></msub><msubsup><mi>V</mi><msub><mi>g</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><mo>⊤</mo></msubsup><mo>+</mo><msubsup><mi>σ</mi><mi>u</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msubsup><msub><mi>I</mi><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>g</mi></msub></msub><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">U_{i}\mid Z,V\;\sim\;\mathcal{N}\!\left(\Lambda_{i}^{-1}\!\!\!\sum_{j:(i,j)\in\mathcal{O}}\!\!\!V_{g_{j}}Z_{ij},\;\;\Lambda_{i}^{-1}\right),\qquad\Lambda_{i}=\!\!\!\sum_{j:(i,j)\in\mathcal{O}}\!\!\!V_{g_{j}}V_{g_{j}}^{\top}+\sigma_{u}^{-2}I_{d_{g}},</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(11)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A4.SS1.p1.3" class="ltx_p">and the symmetric update for <math id="A4.SS1.p1.m15" class="ltx_Math" alttext="V_{g_{j}}\mid Z,U" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>V</mi><msub><mi>g</mi><mi>j</mi></msub></msub><mo fence="false">|</mo><mrow><mi>Z</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>U</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">V_{g_{j}}\mid Z,U</annotation></semantics></math>. Unobserved pairs drop out of
these sums, so the fit is a matrix <em id="A4.SS1.p1.3.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">completion</em> rather than an imputation of
zeros. We run <math id="A4.SS1.p1.m16" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2{,}000" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>2,000</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2{,}000</annotation></semantics></math> iterations, discard the first <math id="A4.SS1.p1.m17" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1{,}000" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>1,000</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1{,}000</annotation></semantics></math> as burn-in, thin
by <math id="A4.SS1.p1.m18" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>2</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2</annotation></semantics></math>, and set <math id="A4.SS1.p1.m19" class="ltx_Math" alttext="V_{g_{j}}\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{g}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>V</mi><msub><mi>g</mi><mi>j</mi></msub></msub><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>g</mi></msub></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">V_{g_{j}}\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{g}}</annotation></semantics></math> with <math id="A4.SS1.p1.m20" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d_{g}=K=10" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>g</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mi>K</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>10</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d_{g}=K=10</annotation></semantics></math> to the posterior
mean of the retained samples. Genes absent from the factorization receive
<math id="A4.SS1.p1.m21" class="ltx_Math" alttext="V_{g}=\mathbf{0}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>V</mi><mi>g</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>𝟎</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">V_{g}=\mathbf{0}</annotation></semantics></math> and a static bias <math id="A4.SS1.p1.m22" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{logit}(\hat{p}_{g})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>logit</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>p</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>g</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{logit}(\hat{p}_{g})</annotation></semantics></math> at their marginal
hit frequency; genes covered by the fit carry no per-gene bias at initialization, so their score is
the pure bilinear form <math id="A4.SS1.p1.m23" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{u}^{\top}V_{g}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mover accent="true"><mi>u</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo>⊤</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>V</mi><mi>g</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{u}^{\top}V_{g}</annotation></semantics></math> and all ranking signal must come
from the screen latent <math id="A4.SS1.p1.m24" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{u}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mover accent="true"><mi>u</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{u}</annotation></semantics></math> that <span id="A4.SS1.p1.3.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">AssayFormer</span> infers in context.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A4.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">D.2 </span>GRPO</h3>

<div id="A4.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Advantages are calculated as the
remaining returns <math id="A4.SS2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="G_{t}^{(i)}=\sum_{s\geq t}r_{s}^{(i)}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>G</mi><mi>t</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>i</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo rspace="0.111em">=</mo><mrow><msub><mo>∑</mo><mrow><mi>s</mi><mo>≥</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow></msub><msubsup><mi>r</mi><mi>s</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>i</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">G_{t}^{(i)}=\sum_{s\geq t}r_{s}^{(i)}</annotation></semantics></math> and normalized across the
group at each step, <math id="A4.SS2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="A_{t}^{(i)}=(G_{t}^{(i)}-\mu_{t})/\sigma_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>A</mi><mi>t</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>i</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi>G</mi><mi>t</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>i</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>μ</mi><mi>t</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>/</mo><msub><mi>σ</mi><mi>t</mi></msub></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">A_{t}^{(i)}=(G_{t}^{(i)}-\mu_{t})/\sigma_{t}</annotation></semantics></math>.
The policy is then updated by the REINFORCE gradient of the Plackett–Luce log-probabilities weighted by <math id="A4.SS2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="A_{t}^{(i)}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>A</mi><mi>t</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>i</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">A_{t}^{(i)}</annotation></semantics></math>, with an entropy bonus (coef <math id="A4.SS2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.01" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.01</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.01</annotation></semantics></math>).
Notably, the learned policy during RL acquires from and is evaluated on the full gene universe (including genes without hit labels in the given screen), so the policy learns to rank the full candidate space, not just each screen’s library.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A4.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">D.3 </span>Training settings</h3>

<div id="A4.SS3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.SS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">In the SFT phase, <span id="A4.SS3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">AssayFormer</span> was trained for 40 epochs with a batch size of 32 screens, AdamW, lr=<math id="A4.SS3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="3e-4" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mn>3</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>e</mi></mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3e-4</annotation></semantics></math>, and weight decay <math id="A4.SS3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1e-2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>e</mi></mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1e-2</annotation></semantics></math>. Gene embeddings were initialized by BPMF (<math id="A4.SS3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d_{g}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>g</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d_{g}</annotation></semantics></math>=10) and left trainable (with no weight decay). The best validation epoch was selected for post-training. It was post-trained with GRPO across 4 B200 GPUs for 100 epochs with group size 8, <math id="A4.SS3.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\gamma=1.0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>γ</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1.0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\gamma=1.0</annotation></semantics></math>, temperature 1.0. There were (<math id="A4.SS3.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\text{floor}(1349/4)=337" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mtext>floor</mtext><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>1349</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>337</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\text{floor}(1349/4)=337</annotation></semantics></math>) steps per epoch. Rollouts were conducted using the universe of genes appearing in two or more screens (21,147 genes, same as evaluation). The context delta reward was used, with the frozen policy <math id="A4.SS3.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pi_{0}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>π</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi_{0}</annotation></semantics></math> updated to the current policy every 25 epochs. Training used AdamW with kl_coef 0.0, ent_coef 0.01, lr 1e-5, weight decay 0.0, grad-norm clipping to 1.0. This resulted in 1348 (<math id="A4.SS3.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\lfloor" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo stretchy="false">⌊</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lfloor</annotation></semantics></math> training set size <math id="A4.SS3.p1.m8" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="/4\rfloor\times 4" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>/</mo><mn>4</mn><mo rspace="0.055em" stretchy="false">⌋</mo><mo rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">/4\rfloor\times 4</annotation></semantics></math>) * 8 (group size) * 100 (epochs) = 1,078,400 traces during training. This is equivalent to 10,784,000 rounds of active learning and 1,078,400,000 genes acquired. We selected a final model checkpoint used in test-set evaluation was selected using validation handoff performance.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A4.SS4" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">D.4 </span><span id="A4.SS4.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">AssayLLM</span></h3>

<section id="A4.SS4.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Backbone.</h5>

<div id="A4.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Qwen3.6-27B, a dense <math id="A4.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="27" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>27</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">27</annotation></semantics></math>B open-weight model with hybrid
linear/full attention. Training uses SDPA attention throughout (FlashAttention-2
is numerically unstable for this architecture on our accelerators) and therefore
no sequence packing. All stages use <span id="A4.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">bf16</span> parameters with DeepSpeed
ZeRO-3; ZeRO-2 exceeds host memory for a model of this size.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A4.SS4.SSS1" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection">D.4.1 </span>SFT</h4>

<section id="A4.SS4.SSS1.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Trajectory construction.</h5>

<div id="A4.SS4.SSS1.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.SS4.SSS1.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Teacher runs are <math id="A4.SS4.SSS1.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>T</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T</annotation></semantics></math>-round campaigns, one
row per (run, screen, round). We reassemble them into single multi-turn
conversations: a shared system prompt describing the goal, screen context,
objective, hit definition, ranking criteria, and required output format; a
<math id="A4.SS4.SSS1.Px1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t{=}1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t{=}1</annotation></semantics></math> user turn carrying the screen description <math id="A4.SS4.SSS1.Px1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="c_{s}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>c</mi><mi>s</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c_{s}</annotation></semantics></math>; then, per round, an
assistant turn holding reasoning traces, an answer <math id="A4.SS4.SSS1.Px1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="B_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>B</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">B_{t}</annotation></semantics></math> as a ranked comma-separated list of <math id="A4.SS4.SSS1.Px1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="b{=}100" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>b</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>100</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">b{=}100</annotation></semantics></math> genes,
and a user turn holding incremental feedback. Feedback lists the labels newly
added to <math id="A4.SS4.SSS1.Px1.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>h</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h_{t}</annotation></semantics></math>, the running cumulative counts, and a non-repetition instruction.
Rows whose assistant body is not a clean gene list are dropped (roughly <math id="A4.SS4.SSS1.Px1.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="3\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>3</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3\%</annotation></semantics></math>).
Only assistant tokens are unmasked in the loss.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A4.SS4.SSS1.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Optimization.</h5>

<div id="A4.SS4.SSS1.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.SS4.SSS1.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Full-parameter fine-tuning across <math id="A4.SS4.SSS1.Px2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="16" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>16</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">16</annotation></semantics></math> GPUs with ZeRO-3, gradient checkpointing, and SDPA attention;
<math id="A4.SS4.SSS1.Px2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="3" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>3</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3</annotation></semantics></math> epochs, global batch size <math id="A4.SS4.SSS1.Px2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="32" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>32</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">32</annotation></semantics></math>, learning rate
<math id="A4.SS4.SSS1.Px2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1{\times}10^{-6}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>6</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1{\times}10^{-6}</annotation></semantics></math> with <math id="A4.SS4.SSS1.Px2.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="3\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>3</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3\%</annotation></semantics></math> warmup.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="A4.SS4.SSS2" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection">D.4.2 </span>GRPO</h4>

<section id="A4.SS4.SSS2.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Rollout.</h5>

<div id="A4.SS4.SSS2.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.SS4.SSS2.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">One prompt is one screen. The policy generates
<math id="A4.SS4.SSS2.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="B_{1},\ldots,B_{k}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>B</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>B</mi><mi>k</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">B_{1},\ldots,B_{k}</annotation></semantics></math> with reasoning enabled; after each round the environment parses
the gene list, reveals <math id="A4.SS4.SSS2.Px1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="y_{g}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>y</mi><mi>g</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y_{g}</annotation></semantics></math> for picks in <math id="A4.SS4.SSS2.Px1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{G}_{s}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒢</mi><mi>s</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{G}_{s}</annotation></semantics></math>, and appends the
incremental feedback turn. Group size is <math id="A4.SS4.SSS2.Px1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="16" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>16</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">16</annotation></semantics></math> samples per prompt, sampled at
temperature <math id="A4.SS4.SSS2.Px1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1.0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>1.0</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1.0</annotation></semantics></math> and top-<math id="A4.SS4.SSS2.Px1.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p\,0.95" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mn> 0.95</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p\,0.95</annotation></semantics></math>; higher diversity is useful here because
group-relative advantages need within-group spread.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A4.SS4.SSS2.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Optimization.</h5>

<div id="A4.SS4.SSS2.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.SS4.SSS2.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We then optimize the policy with Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO). For each prompt <math id="A4.SS4.SSS2.Px2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>x</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x</annotation></semantics></math> we sample a group of <math id="A4.SS4.SSS2.Px2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="G" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>G</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">G</annotation></semantics></math> responses <math id="A4.SS4.SSS2.Px2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\{y_{i}\}_{i=1}^{G}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>G</mi></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\{y_{i}\}_{i=1}^{G}</annotation></semantics></math> from the current policy
and compute the group-normalized advantage</p>
<table id="A4.E12" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A4.E12.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{A}_{i}\;=\;\frac{r_{i}-\mathrm{mean}(\{r_{j}\}_{j=1}^{G})}{\mathrm{std}(\{r_{j}\}_{j=1}^{G})}," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>A</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>i</mi></msub><mo lspace="0.558em" rspace="0.558em">=</mo><mfrac><mrow><msub><mi>r</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>−</mo><mrow><mi>mean</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msubsup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><msub><mi>r</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>j</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>G</mi></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mrow><mi>std</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msubsup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><msub><mi>r</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>j</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>G</mi></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mfrac></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{A}_{i}\;=\;\frac{r_{i}-\mathrm{mean}(\{r_{j}\}_{j=1}^{G})}{\mathrm{std}(\{r_{j}\}_{j=1}^{G})},</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(12)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A4.SS4.SSS2.Px2.p1.2" class="ltx_p">and maximize the clipped surrogate objective</p>
<table id="A4.E13" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A4.E13.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\mathcal{J}(\theta)=\mathbb{E}\!\left[\frac{1}{G}\sum_{i=1}^{G}\min\!\Big(\rho_{i}\hat{A}_{i},\;\mathrm{clip}(\rho_{i},1-\epsilon,1+\epsilon)\hat{A}_{i}\Big)\right]-\beta\,\mathbb{D}_{\mathrm{KL}}\!\left(\pi_{\theta}\,\|\,\pi_{\mathrm{ref}}\right)," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒥</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mpadded style="width:0.497em;" width="0.497em"><mi>𝔼</mi></mpadded><mrow><mo>[</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mi>G</mi></mfrac><munderover><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>G</mi></munderover><mpadded style="width:1.653em;" width="1.653em"><mi>min</mi></mpadded><mrow><mo maxsize="1.600em" minsize="1.600em">(</mo><msub><mi>ρ</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>A</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>i</mi></msub><mo rspace="0.447em">,</mo><mi>clip</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>ρ</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>ϵ</mi><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mi>ϵ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>A</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>i</mi></msub><mo maxsize="1.600em" minsize="1.600em">)</mo></mrow><mo>]</mo></mrow><mo>−</mo><mi>β</mi><msub><mi>𝔻</mi><mi>KL</mi></msub><mrow><mo>(</mo><msub><mi>π</mi><mi>θ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.337em">∥</mo><msub><mi>π</mi><mi>ref</mi></msub><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{J}(\theta)=\mathbb{E}\!\left[\frac{1}{G}\sum_{i=1}^{G}\min\!\Big(\rho_{i}\hat{A}_{i},\;\mathrm{clip}(\rho_{i},1-\epsilon,1+\epsilon)\hat{A}_{i}\Big)\right]-\beta\,\mathbb{D}_{\mathrm{KL}}\!\left(\pi_{\theta}\,\|\,\pi_{\mathrm{ref}}\right),</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
